GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning

Quick read

ICLR 2026 Oral from Khattab/Zaharia/Stoica/Klein/Sen/Dimakis/Potts (DSPy crew). A prompt optimizer that uses natural-language reflection on trajectories as the gradient signal instead of policy gradients on scalar rewards. Across 6 tasks: beats GRPO by 6% avg / 20% max with 35× fewer rollouts. Beats prior prompt-optimizer SOTA (MIPROv2) by >10%.

How it works

For an AI system built from one or more LLM prompts: 1. Sample trajectories on the task. 2. LLM reflects on failed trajectories in natural language — diagnoses what went wrong, proposes specific prompt edits. 3. Test the proposed prompt on a small batch. 4. Maintain a Pareto frontier of prompt variants — different prompts win on different sub-distributions of the task. Don't collapse to one best. 5. Use a genetic operator to combine complementary lessons from frontier prompts into new candidates. 6. Iterate.

The core philosophical claim: a scalar reward is one bit per rollout; a natural-language critique is hundreds of bits per rollout. For matched compute budget, reflection-based search extracts much more signal per sample.

Why it matters to our work

Direct application: optimize the consolidator prompt with GEPA instead of GRPO. See Goal 01 for the active experiment.

If GEPA matches Auto-Dreamer's quality at 1/35th the compute, the practical implication is huge: consolidation training becomes laptop-budget instead of 8× H100. See Goal 02 for that downstream experiment.

What it can't do

  • Change model knowledge or fundamental capability
  • Train models for non-verifiable open-ended generation
  • Run during deployment (offline optimizer, like any)
